title: Probabilistic Consumption Uncertainty Resolver and Late-Arrival Credit Orchestrator
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently have two failure modes that lead to incorrect tenant balances: (1) out-of-order/late ingestion of token consumption events from edge gateways and regional relays, and (2) ambiguous attribution when requests cross multi-model routes or fallback chains. These root causes result in either duplicated charges or missed credits after backfills.

Goal: Implement a probabilistic uncertainty resolver that assigns confidence scores to consumption records, integrates with the existing epochal watermarking window, and issues retroactive credit adjustments in an idempotent, auditable way. The system should reduce manual billing corrections, maintain SLA for near-real-time invoicing, and be resilient to high-throughput spikes during deploys.

Scope: Build a standalone orchestrator job that: (a) computes an uncertainty score per consumption event using deterministic heuristics + lightweight model features, (b) consolidates overlapping late-arrival events within a bounded time window, (c) produces credit/charge transactions routed to the ledger in an idempotent fashion (with conflict resolution using event provenance), and (d) exposes metrics and tracing for post-mortem reconciliation and customer questions.
acceptance_criteria: Uncertainty scoring implemented and persisted for all consumption events in the staging replay (>= 99.8% coverage)
Retroactive credit/charge operations are idempotent and include provenance metadata linked to original events
End-to-end pipeline reduces manual billing corrections by >= 60% in the replayed historical dataset
Job observes SLO: processing latency for a typical daily window <= 10 minutes for 95th percentile (on dedicated runner)
Metrics and dashboarding: uncertainty distribution, retro credit volume, false-positive rate and reconciliation failures visible in console
